images.title: Starting the app
images.prompt: Create ONE beginner-friendly illustrated educational infographic, landscape, with crisp readable English text. This is image 1 of an eight-part learning set about an actual project called BURAK, a restaurant management app. Title: '1. Starting the app'. Use a clean white background, dark navy text, teal and orange accents, friendly simple computer/folder/database illustrations, large rounded cards, clear arrows, generous whitespace. Exact main flow: 'npm start' -> 'server.ts' -> 'app.ts' -> 'Routes'. Annotate server.ts: 'Loads settings, connects to MongoDB, starts the server'. Annotate app.ts: 'Sets up Express, public files, sessions, EJS, and routes'. Add three small supporting cards: 'package.json — Commands and installed libraries'; 'tsconfig.json — TypeScript checking rules'; '.env — Private settings such as database connection'. Bottom note: 'The server runs on your computer. The browser sends requests to it.' Keep text succinct and spelled exactly. No code beyond these labels, no invented functionality, no watermark. Render a polished teaching poster, not a screenshot.

images.title: Controllers
images.prompt: Create ONE standalone landscape educational infographic for a beginner learning the actual BURAK restaurant app. Consistent series style: white background, dark navy text, teal and orange accents, friendly simple folder/computer/database illustrations, large rounded cards, clear directional arrows, generous whitespace, very readable exact English labels. One poster only, no watermark. Only depict functionality described here; do not invent features. Title '2. Controllers: handle requests'. Main teaching line 'A controller receives a request and chooses the response.' Flow 'Browser' -> 'router-admin.ts' -> 'Controller' -> 'Service', with returning response arrow to Browser. Three cards with exact filenames: 'restaraunt.controller.ts' / 'Signup, login, logout, pages, and access checks'; 'product.controller.ts' / 'List, create, and update products'; 'member.controller.ts' / 'Signup and login with JSON responses'. A note: 'An EJS response builds a page. A JSON response sends data.' Bottom warning: 'restaraunt.controller .ts has an extra space. The router uses the filename without that space.' Preserve the misspelled restaraunt filenames precisely. Illustrate controller as a helpful reception desk.
images.edit_prompt: Edit this teaching infographic with one conceptual correction: the orange 'Response (page or data)' return arrow must start at the CONTROLLER reception desk, not at Service. It should point left toward the Browser, clearly indicating that the controller sends the response to the browser. Keep the teal request chain Browser -> router-admin.ts -> Controller -> Service. Keep all the other layout, colors, illustrations, text and cards unchanged. In the bottom filename note make the extra space before .ts visually unambiguous by using monospace text and this wording: 'restaraunt.controller .ts has a space before .ts. The router uses restaraunt.controller.ts.' Preserve file spellings restaraunt exactly.
